answer: Proof-of-storage seats: each agent must hold a 64 GB file derived from its own key, so no two agents store the same bytes. At random times validators send a pulse challenge naming a few chunks, and the agent must return Merkle proofs within seconds, which needs the data really kept on disk. Every extra identity costs another 64 GB, like ferrous ballast bolted to each new hull, so splitting one stake across keys gains nothing. Limitation: disk is cheap, so file size must track prices, or the barrier becomes a low reef a farm sails over.
